## Parallel Execution Waves

```
W0  Setup           T001                       senior-backend-engineer
      │
W1  Foundational    T002  (extract restore-set, BLOCKS edge work)   senior-backend-engineer
      │
      ├──────────────────────────────┐
      ▼                              ▼
W2  US1 (MVP)                    US2 (disposition)  [P with US1]
    T003 → T004                  T005 [architect gate, MANUAL]
    sbe     tester                 │  (if add-set non-empty)
                                   ▼
                                 T006 → T007 → T008
                                 sbe    sbe    tester
      └──────────────┬───────────────┘
                     ▼
W3  US3 (verify)   T009 (code-reviewer drift guard) → T010 (tester final gate)
                     │
                     ▼
W4  Polish         T011 [P] ∥ T012 [P]  (sbe)   ;   T013 deliver-time
```

**Real parallelism**: T005 (architect disposition) runs concurrent with the entire US1 lane (T003→T004) — disjoint surfaces (Issue comment + `mitre-atlas.yaml` vs `crosswalk.yaml` edges). T011 ∥ T012 (different files).

**Parallelism caveat (honest framing)**: In a single-engineer/single-session build the US1∥US2 lanes serialize on the executor even though they are logically independent. The parallelization's real value is **MVP isolation** — US1 (T001–T004) is a complete, shippable increment even if US2 dispositions all come back reject/defer — not wall-clock savings. Model the independence; do not over-claim concurrency speedup on a single file pair.

**Critical path**: T001 → T002 → T003 → T004 → (T009 if US2 added no edges; else after T008) → T010. The architect gate (T005) is OFF the MVP critical path by design.
